title: Regional Transmission Engineering Manager
description:
Xcel Energy (NASDAQ: XEL) is a leading energy provider and Fortune 500 company, dedicated to serving millions of electricity and natural gas customers across eight states: Minnesota, Colorado, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota, New Mexico and Texas. We make energy work better for our customers, helping them thrive every day. That means always raising the bar - delivering better service and providing more reliable, resilient, and sustainable energy.

Xcel Energy is a place where you’ll have opportunities to grow, expand your skills, and help lead the clean energy transition. We offer meaningful rewards, recognition, and support to help you build your career and make an impact - both on the job and beyond. Most importantly, it means you’ll be joining a company that knows employees are the driving force behind its success and is committed to helping you be your best.

Xcel Energy supports a hybrid work model to enable collaboration and flexibility. Many roles are expected to work onsite three days per week (Tuesday–Thursday); however, work location expectations vary based on role, team, and business needs.
Position Summary

Responsible for the development of the strategic direction on Regional Transmission Planning matters that support the company's operational and financial goals through leadership and coordination with other company business areas. Develop the policy direction and recommendations relating to Regional Transmission Planning system implementation. Deploy and maintain Xcel Energy's representation on strategic committees and work groups to ensure external influence on Regional Transmission Planning and Regional Reliability Organization (RRO) developments. Develop and deliver presentations to senior management, regulatory, and industry related to Regional Transmission Planning development and Xcel Energy's system implementation. Represent company's interests at the Regional Transmission Planning Policy and Board committees level. Coordinate Transmission Operations, Metering Data Management Agent, and Business Systems with Energy Markets, and Settlements on Regional Transmission Planning matters. Deliver expertise on Regional Transmission Planning and RRO issues in this rapidly changing sector of the industry.

Essential Responsibilities

- Identify impacts of Regional Transmission Planning initiatives (competitive, environmental, structural) on transmission and corporate positions in a timely manner. Develop and coordinate transmission strategy on Regional Transmission Planning matters to the point where they are supported by senior management for Transmission, Energy Markets, and Regulatory. Provides timely and continuous Regional Transmission Planning related information to business units to insure consistency with corporate positions and strategies. Execute strategies externally for advancing the company's position.

- Prepare and review of written and oral internal and external reports, comments, and briefing materials on transmission related policy matters.

- Work directly with management throughout Xcel Energy to develop and promote transmission policy positions consistent with corporate goals. Develop, direct and coordinate transmission related regulatory activities at both the state and federal level associated with changing reliability and market rules. Advocate Transmission's position both internally and externally to senior management, regulators, stakeholders and leadership of Regional Transmission Planning. Perform other duties as necessary to promote regional transmission policy requirements. Seek to transform transmission policy stakeholder relationships into strategic assets by creating a climate of mutual understanding, trust, and support.

- Serves as project manager for developing and implementing initiatives resulting from Regional Transmission Planningpolicy changes. Act as coordinator for the system reliability and readiness around Regional Transmission Planning participation, as well as, ensuring systems are in place for cost recovery.

- Regularly communicate, both written and orally, with senior management and internal customers to ensure awareness of current Regional Transmission Planning and reliability issues that impact Xcel Energy's operations as well as strong awareness of business acumen. Interact with regulators, stakeholders, and internal customers to identify and proactively pursue results that support Xcel Energy's policies and goals regarding matters such as transmission open access, standard of conduct policy issues, and cost recovery.

Minimum Requirements

- BA/BS in engineering, business, economics, or related discipline or a combination of education and experience providing equivalent knowledge.

- Minimum of 10 years progressive operations and regulatory experience in the electric energy industry, including a minimum of 4 years experience working with Regional Transmission or Reliability Organizations agencies.

- Strong business acumen and sense of urgency.

- Must be proactive, adept at working with other utility executives, regulatory agencies, and capable of making decisions in a rapidly changing and demanding environment.

- Ability to identify specific opportunities with Regional Transmission Planning.

- Knowledge of market aspects of Regional Transmission Planning. Knowledge of tariff administration.

- Advanced organizational, communications, leadership, and analytical skills.

- Ability to use MS-Office applications (e.g., Word, Excel).

- Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex information.

- Ability to work hours in excess of 40 per week.

- Ability to travel overnight on a regular basis.

- Selection criteria may include testing and/or assessment.

Preferred Requirements

- Electrical Engineer with Power Systems background.

- Experience in Western Electricity Markets.

- Stakeholder Engagement Leadership.

description:

Position Summary

Join Xcel Energy as a Transmission Production Cost Modeling Analyst and play a pivotal role in shaping the future of our electric power system! Prepare and direct economic transmission planning efforts using PROMOD and other tools to serve Xcel Energy's electric power system planning functions serving native customer demand and energy requirements to support regulatory filing, reduce customer costs and meet corporate budgeting requirements. Support the preparation of direct testimony for regulatory proceedings and provide responses to regulatory agencies information requests pertaining to wholesale energy market plans related to the transmission system. Investigate and develop new techniques to improve economic transmission planning processes. Support transmission planning work including evaluation of interregional projects and congestion cost mitigation opportunities.

Essential Responsibilities

- Assist in development of energy market forecasts for electric transmission development to support long range plans, regulatory filings, and reduce congestion. Support development of direct testimony for regulatory proceedings. Work with senior modelers to provide responses to regulatory agencies information requests pertaining to wholesale energy market-based plans and modeling of Xcel Energy's transmission system. Direct independent analyses to respond to or support regulatory agencies review of Xcel Energy's transmission system.

- Support the develop production cost inputs into transmission modeling for electric system planning purposes. Produce electric system production cost uploads needed within Integrated System Planning. Prepare forecasts of off system impacts to congestion and curtailment.

- Work with senior Modelers to perform electric system transmission modeling analyses to independently evaluate activities of Xcel Energy's operating companies, from a Risk Management perspective, pertaining to transmission assets, regional planning processes, competitive transmission development, transmission and environmental issues. Prepare independent evaluations of regional transmission plans, and initiate analysis of existing and new transmission system limitations.

- Perform monthly assessment of resource congestion and curtailment. Support responses to regulatory group and state regulatory agencies requests and questions.

- Investigate and develop new techniques to improve economic transmission planning processes.

- Maintain and verify all input data as necessary for the transmission production cost modeling team. Ensure transmission and generation system data is available to accurately modeled in terms of ratings, flow gates, fuel costs, production capability (heat rates, capacity, VOM, etc.) and contract terms in order to provide accurate analysis of transmission system impacts. Optimize existing and develop new programs to post process output.

Minimum Requirements

- Bachelor's of Science or Bachelor's of Arts degree in electrical engineering, economics, mathematics, physics, quantitative analysis, business or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

- At least 5 years of experience in analyzing transmission systems including 3 years of experience in wholesale energy markets using financial tools/production simulation software.

- Must have advanced quantitative analysis skills and extensive knowledge in the systems and software required for such analyses.

Preferred Requirements

- Experience with Production Cost Modeling software or equivalent.

- Advanced skills using spreadsheet and database software.

- Extensive knowledge of the performance, operations, and modeling of assets, preferably Xcel Energy's assets.

description:
Are you looking for an exciting job where you can put your skills and talents to work at a company you can feel proud to be a part of? Do you want a workplace that will challenge you and offer you opportunities to learn and grow?  A   position at Xcel Energy could be just what you’re looking for.

Position Summary

Apply diversified knowledge to determine the appropriate policy direction and develop recommendations for the company's physical security regulatory compliance with Federal, State and local jurisdictions. Consult with regulatory and subject matter experts throughout the company and industry to establish progressive and consistent policies, procedures, programs to meet mandatory regulatory compliance. Prepare and deliver supporting testimony in Federal, State and local regulatory proceedings, administrative rulemaking as necessary. Coordinate physical security regulatory compliance activities in assigned jurisdictions.

This person will need to be based in our SPS territory - western Texas/eastern New Mexico.

Essential Responsibilities

- Develop and coordinate physical security regulatory programs, policies, procedures s based on mandates issued by Federal, State and local government. Coordinate regulatory filings and associated data requests for multiple jurisdictions concurrently.

- Identify impacts of regulatory initiatives on company facilities from state-specific to national perspectives. Conduct internal assessment activities including training, spot checks and reviews to ensure compliance. Facilitate project activities as needed to address identified gaps.

- Continuously interact with regulators, stakeholders and internal customers to identify and proactively pursue results that reflect the company's regulatory policies and strategies of physical security mandates, policies and initiatives

- Advocate the company's positions with regulators and stakeholders in a variety of forums (e.g. regulatory proceedings, administrative rulemaking, hearings, councils, industry organizations, etc.) Advocate physical security policies in assigned jurisdictions that are consistent with company policies in other jurisdictions. Maintain oversight of regulatory rulemaking activities in assigned jurisdictions and provide written and oral comments to prepare and deliver supporting testimony as required.

- Perform field inventory of Physical Security technology required by regulatory and contractual compliance as well as any internally identified procedures assigned related to inventory of assets. Assist in Physical Security investigations as required.

- Serve as liaison with internal regulatory departments. Manage audits with internal departments and provide Enterprise Security management with findings. Maintain physical security control documentation and tracking of physical security projects at assets to ensure that standard requirements around physical security are maintained.

Minimum Requirements

- Completion of a four year academic degree, preferably in Security Management, Criminal Justice or Business Administration or a combination of other relevant security education.

- Minimum of 10 years of industrial security experience in a corporate environment, with extensive knowledge of the electric, gas, and/or hydroelectric energy sectors. Equivalent experience in utility operations and physical security regulatory compliance will also be considered.

- 8 years regulatory project management and experience developing and managing security requirements to meet Federal, State and Local government mandates.

This position can be hired at the Entry, Staff, or Senior level, depending on the candidates' overall experience, qualifications, and interview. This position will be based in Denver, Colorado on a hybrid (3 days per week in the office) work schedule.

Key Job Performance Criteria (will differ based upon job level)
Perform Comprehensive Power System Planning Studies, including:

- Steady-State Load Flow Analysis under normal and contingency conditions (N-1, N-1-1, and extreme events) to identify system limitations and develop mitigation strategies.

- Short-Circuit and Protection Coordination Studies to ensure appropriate equipment ratings, relay coordination, and breaker duty compliance, including assessments for system modifications and new interconnections.

- Dynamic Performance Assessments, including Transient Stability and Small-Signal Stability Studies to evaluate rotor angle stability, voltage recovery, and oscillatory damping performance under a wide range of system disturbances.

- Electromagnetic Transient (EMT) Analysis for evaluating control interactions and fast dynamic phenomena associated with large power electronic loads (e.g., data centers), inverter-based resources (IBRs), and FACTS devices, leveraging PSCAD/EMTDC.

- Geomagnetic Induced Current (GIC) Studies aligned with NERC TPL-007 standards to assess geomagnetic disturbance impacts on transformers and bulk electric system reliability.

Support Regulatory Compliance and Model Validation Activities:

- Perform NERC TPL-001-5.1 compliance assessments, including extreme event analyses such as CIP-014 physical security risk assessments, wide-area event simulations, and black start restoration studies.

- Support dynamic model validation efforts per WECC and NERC MOD standards, ensuring fidelity of generator, inverter, and composite load models for stability studies.

Conduct Advanced Inverter-Based Resource (IBR) Integration Studies:

- Assess grid-forming/grid-following inverter technologies and their impact on system strength, transient behavior, and control interactions.

- Apply IEEE 2800 requirements for IBR performance, including ride-through, reactive power support, and fast frequency response capabilities.

- Address challenges of high renewable penetration and develop mitigation strategies to maintain bulk power system reliability.

Support Western Interconnection and Regional Planning:

- Coordinate with WestConnect Planning Management Committee, WECC Reliability Subcommittees, and interconnection working groups to support transmission expansion planning, regional policy compliance, and reliability initiatives.

- Engage in regional and subregional transmission planning processes, contributing to multi-utility studies and cross-border resource integration scenarios.

Perform Resource Interconnection and Transmission Service Studies:

- Execute System Impact Studies (SIS) and Facility Studies consistent with FERC Order 2023 and regional tariffs.

- Evaluate interconnection requests for conventional generation, IBRs, storage, hybrid resources, and emerging technologies such as microgrids and aggregated DERs under FERC 2222 frameworks.

- Recommend necessary transmission reinforcements, upgrades, or operational solutions to accommodate new resources and loads.

Evaluate Grid-Enhancing Technologies (GETs):

- Analyze and model Dynamic Line Rating (DLR), Advanced Power Flow Controllers (APFC), and Topology Optimization (TTO) to maximize transmission efficiency and capacity without traditional infrastructure expansion.

- Support cost-benefit assessments and pilot project implementations for GETs in collaboration with operations and asset management teams.

Automation and Digitalization:

- Develop and maintain Python-based automation tools to streamline study execution, scenario management, and results post-processing for PSSE, PSLF, TARA, TSAT, PSCAD simulations.

- Advance digital workflows to reduce engineering effort, improve repeatability, and enable high-volume interconnection and compliance studies.

Reporting, Regulatory Filings, and Knowledge Dissemination:

- Author and deliver technical reports, regulatory filings, and executive summaries for internal leadership and external regulatory agencies.

- Present findings at regional stakeholder meetings, industry conferences (e.g., IEEE PES, CIGRÉ), and technical workshops to communicate planning approaches and emerging challenges.

Industry Engagement and Representation:

- Represent Xcel Energy in NERC working groups, IEEE technical committees, WECC Model Validation Working Group, WestConnect Planning forums, and other industry task forces focused on dynamic performance, renewable integration, and bulk power system reliability.

Mentorship and Technical Leadership:

- Mentor engineers, interns, and analysts on advanced simulation methodologies, IBR modeling, EMT techniques, and emerging grid technologies.

- Provide technical leadership to internal teams, fostering expertise development in grid dynamics, automation, and planning best practices.

-  Lead internal technical workshops and contribute to the development of best-in-class planning documentation and standards.

- Support development of capital budgets, conceptual transmission projects, and economic analyses in joint planning contexts.

Join Xcel Energy’s PSCo Transmission Planning team in Denver, Colorado, and work on some of the most technically challenging and strategically significant power system issues facing the electric industry today. This internship provides a unique opportunity for Master's and Ph.D. students to apply advanced power systems knowledge in a real utility environment where planning decisions directly influence grid reliability, large-load integration, renewable energy development, grid modernization, and long-term transmission investment across Colorado and the broader Western Interconnection.

As a member of the Transmission Planning team, you will work alongside experienced engineers and recognized subject matter experts performing steady-state, dynamic stability, and electromagnetic transient (EMT) studies that support both near-term operational reliability and long-term grid expansion. Interns gain hands-on experience with industry-leading software platforms including PSS®E, PSLF, TARA, DSATools, and PSCAD while developing and validating transmission models, evaluating system performance under stressed conditions, assessing contingency events, analyzing large-load interconnections, and studying the behavior of inverter-based resources and emerging grid technologies.

The team is actively engaged in high-profile initiatives involving hyperscale data centers, renewable energy integration, advanced transmission technologies, grid-enhancing technologies (GETs), transmission expansion planning, system reliability assessments, and interconnection studies. Interns will have the opportunity to contribute to projects addressing some of the industry's most important challenges, including power system stability, system strength, frequency response, resource adequacy, transmission congestion, and the evolution of the modern electric grid.

In addition to technical studies, interns may support strategic initiatives and research efforts associated with U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) programs and funding opportunities focused on advanced transmission technologies, grid modernization, resilience, and decarbonization. The internship also emphasizes technical thought leadership. Interns will be encouraged to conduct independent research, develop technical white papers, and contribute to conference-quality publications intended for presentation at leading industry forums such as IEEE conferences, CIGRE, ESIG, and other professional organizations. This provides a rare opportunity to bridge academic research with real-world utility applications while building a strong professional publication record.

Interns will collaborate closely with transmission planning, operations, protection, modeling, and engineering groups while presenting technical findings to engineers, managers, and senior leadership. The experience is designed to provide meaningful exposure to utility-scale power system planning while developing the analytical, modeling, research, and communication skills required for future leadership roles in the electric power industry.

Located in Denver, Colorado, this position offers the opportunity to work with a highly respected team recognized for its technical excellence, innovation, and industry leadership. - Analyze study results and prepare technical reports, presentations, and recommendations to support planning and operational decision-making.

- Collaborate with transmission planning, operations, protection, and modeling teams on projects related to reliability, grid modernization, and large load interconnections.

title: Senior Resource Planning Analyst (or Resource Planning Analyst II or I)
description:
Are you looking for an exciting job where you can put your skills and talents to work at a company you can feel proud to be a part of? Do you want a workplace that will challenge you and offer you opportunities to learn and grow?  A   position at Xcel Energy could be just what you’re looking for.

The job summary below and responsibilities reflect the Senior Resource Planning Analyst role . The successfully chosen candidate will be placed at a level that is commensurate with their skills and experience as different skills and/or experience will be required at the Resource Planning Analyst II and Resource Planning Analyst I levels.

This modeling-focused team is responsible for model development, innovation, testing, and integration with the enterprise data fabric. The team is composed of technical experts in economics, engineering, and mathematics. We are seeking subject matter experts with experience in capacity expansion and production cost analysis, nodal analysis, regional transmission analysis, reliability studies, or operations research related to the electric utility industry.

Position Summary
Model, analyze, and develop resource expansion plans to meet electric system growth requirements for the Xcel operating utility companies. Prepare and perform generation expansion modeling studies. Provide project management for resource solicitations and resource plan development, which requires developing recommendations based on extensive modeling and analysis by an analytical team including outside consultants. Prepare extensive reports for regulators. Present and defend recommendations to senior management. Testify in administrative hearings. Investigate and develop quantitative techniques to improve analytical processes. Be a resource to Resource Planning Analysts. Be the generation planning expert for one of the larger Xcel Energy utilities. Accept responsibility for the most difficult analytical efforts required in the department.

Essential Responsibilities

- Through extensive modeling and other quantitative techniques, develop comprehensive plans to obtain or add new capacity and energy resources (e.g. new generation plants) in the most cost-effective manner. Such plans and processes must be developed for each company and state, within resource planning / acquisition rules that govern the expansion of the system / addition of new generation and/or purchased power resources. Project manage development of these resource plans for larger Xcel Energy operating utilities. Lead team in preparing and performing the modeling studies required to discover the optimal portfolio of generation resources to meet customer energy and peak demand. Such teams are often span 20-30 people across departments are including outside consultants. Recommend plan to senior officers. These recommendations often lead to decisions valued in excess of $1 billion dollars, undergo intense public scrutiny and cost $.5 to 2 million to develop.

- Interface with regulators, interveners, including political and special interest groups, customers, and power suppliers to obtain consensus, support, and/or regulatory approval of optimal resource plans. This includes writing testimony, testifying in administrative hearings, negotiating settlement agreements, presenting plans. It also included gaining acceptance of plans from executive management, regulators and external groups.

- Prepare and perform expansion and production cost economic modeling of alternative supply plans and resources to develop optimal supply-demand portfolios for each Xcel Energy operating utility, incorporating consideration of various risks (e.g. fuel prices, electric market prices, reliability criteria, environmental requirements, technology development scenarios, etc.). Develop new quantitative processes to analyze risk issues.

- Interface and work with Forecasting, Risk Management, Trading, Gas Supply, Coal Supply, Transmission Operations, Regulatory Services, Retail and other Xcel groups to incorporate short-term and long-range considerations into the resource plans, including transmission constraints, growth forecasts, demand side management forecasts, fuel and electricity market price risks, etc.

- In conjunction with Risk Management, ensure that the expansion plan and production cost modeling of the utility power systems is accurate and current in terms of fuel costs, production capability (heat rates, capacity, starting and variable operating cost, etc.), contract terms (scheduling flexibility, constraints, availability, etc.).

- Be an expert resource for at least one of the Xcel Energy utilities. This includes familiarity with all generation and contracts for the utility, with the load and capability tables of the utility, rules and regulations of the states in which the utility operates. It also includes having a network of contacts to gather system information.

- Project manage resource solicitation processes including developing the proposal, overseeing the evaluations conducted by a team of analysts and outside consultants, assuring the process was fair to all parties, recommending and defending winning offers to senior management and defending evaluation processes and recommendations in public and regulatory forums. These solicitations often involve decisions costing in excess of a billion dollars and expenditure of $500,000 to $2,000,000 to conduct the solicitation and selection process.

- Be a resource for less experienced planning analysts in the areas of modeling, problem analysis, regulatory strategy and system knowledge.

Senior Resource Planning Analyst ($112,200 - 159,400)
Minimum Requirements

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, mathematics, economics or quantitative analysis.

- At least eight years utility experience in work functions such as plant engineering or operations, forecasting, rates, load research, or similar function that provides candidate with understanding of generation planning and system modeling techniques.

- At least three years modeling experience with expansion or production simulation models.

- Extensive system knowledge of at least one of the larger Xcel Energy utilities.

-

Resource Planning Analyst II ($97,600-138,600)
​ Minimum Requirements

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, finance, economics, operations research, mathematics, business.

- Five or more years related work experience.

- Graduate work in finance, economics, operations research or decision analysis preferred.

Minimum Requirements

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, finance, economics, operations research, mathematics, business (two years professional experience related experience equivalent to one year of college).
